generic-boilerplate-non-orienting: A heading or field label is technically accurate but so generic ('Information', 'Details', 'Value') that users can't predict what the section contains or what to type.
non-distinct-siblings-relational: Several headings or labels on the page are identical or near-identical ('Description, Description, Description'), so a screen-reader user skimming them can't tell the sections apart.
icon-graphical-label-context: An icon labeling a control is misleading for its real function, like a floppy-disk icon on a 'Send' button or a magnifying glass on a filter button.
label-omits-data-requirements: A field's label names its topic but hides the format it secretly demands (a 'Date' box requiring MM/DD/YYYY), so users can't tell what input is accepted.
ambiguous-button-action-label: A button's text is too vague to reveal what it does, like several 'OK'/'Go' buttons that each behave differently or a 'Continue' button that actually deletes your draft.
descriptiveness-depends-on-layout-or-sta: A heading matches the content right after it in the code, but once CSS reorders the layout or a panel collapses, it ends up over unrelated content.
visible-vs-accessible-name-divergence: The on-screen label and the label a screen reader actually announces disagree (shown as 'First name' but announced as 'field1'), so sighted and screen-reader users get different labels.
